correctness.rationale: The count of checkerboard units for each two-site species pair is 4, 1, or 0 depending on disjoint, singleton-intersection or identical supports. Grouping by ten site-pair types yields a homogeneous quadratic. Its global maximum over the real simplex follows from exact support enumeration of all 1023 faces: 130 positive stationary points with strictly negative tangent Hessians, whose seven value strata have maximum 12/11. Singular maximizing faces reduce along exact flat tangent directions to these candidates; all ten winners have external gradients 17/11 versus 24/11 on support, excluding larger-support equality points. The integer equality condition is 11 dividing species count. The packaged standard-library verifier checks determinants, solves stationary equations over fractions, and confirms 352705 brute-force multisets and both score formulas.

value.rationale: Ecological segregation analysis uses the classical checkerboard C-score, but raw scores change with matrix shape and frequency of site occupancy. At fixed row occupancy exactly two, the sharp upper envelope determines the meaningful scale and all extremal incidence structures for arbitrarily many species over five surveyed habitats. The five-site motif is qualitatively different from the disjoint-block four-site optimum: a fourth occupied pair type forms a triangle among the complementary habitats, and increases the scale-free ceiling from 1 to 12/11. This is structural ecological mathematics, not routine substitution or a claim of null-model significance.
